_comment: Sword readability. THE GAMEPLAY CAMERA IS THE JUDGED FRAME. A previous round passed every showcase angle and failed a fresh critic outright, who identified the one gameplay-camera frame unaided and said of it: 'I cannot find a weapon. Not a pixel of blade.' The three good frames were good because they were shot from angles no player will ever occupy. So the gameplay shots come first here and they are the ones that count: they omit camera_pitch_deg and camera_distance entirely, which capture.gd resolves to player.tscn's own spring arm, and the player faces away as they always do without input. gp_idle is the control — every other gp_ frame must be unmistakably distinguishable from it. Showcase angles follow, kept only for reading pose detail. Shot at (16, -2) rather than the spawn, which is ringed with logs and signs that every swing frame overlapped.
_capture_when: EVERY shot now uses capture_when plus expect_*, and that is a repair, not a preference. This file used to use capture_at frame arithmetic, which capture.gd's own header warns is the wrong contract — the numbers were fitted to a measured three-frame input latency and drift the moment anything upstream changes. They had drifted: the manifest for the last capture_at run showed gp_slash_a_windup captured with state=Idle clip=idle (an idle frame filed as a wind-up), gp_slash_a_live captured mid-transition with clip=idle, gp_slash_a_recover captured with the hitbox still LIVE, and gp_slash_b_live captured during slash_a. Four of ten judged frames were labelled as something they were not, and nothing failed, because capture_at shots carry no expectations. Every shot below says what state it wants and asserts it, so the run exits non-zero rather than handing a critic a mislabelled frame.

shots._note: CONTROL. Identical camera to every other gp_ shot, no input at all.
shots.name: gp_idle

shots._note: The wind-up: the first frame the AnimationTree calls slash_a. This is the frame the critic could only identify by comparing it against its paired idle, so it is deliberately taken at the earliest possible instant rather than a few frames in where the pose has fully arrived. It carries three things now: the frame-0 anticipation pose (which needed trans_attack_in dropped to 0.02 s to survive the blend), the blade gone hot, and the ribbon opened narrow by begin_attack rather than by a keyframe.
shots.name: gp_slash_a_windup

shots._note: slash_a, first live frame: blade out on the right flank, ribbon spanning the descent from above the head.
shots.name: gp_slash_a_live

shots._note: slash_a late in the live window: blade crossing the front, so the arc is carried by the ribbon rather than by the blade.
shots.name: gp_slash_a_live_late

shots._note: slash_a recovery: ten frames past the first live frame, so the 6-frame hitbox window is long closed and the blade is back up on the follow-through. Counted from the live window rather than from the press, because that is the only anchor capture_when offers that stays correct when the clip is retimed. If the arc is gone by here it was never persistent enough to read — with the ribbon shortened to a 12-tick smear this is the frame that proves it did not get too short.
shots.name: gp_slash_a_recover

shots._note: slash_b live, the chained follow-up: rising, blade above the head, the opposite screen direction to slash_a.
shots.name: gp_slash_b_live

shots._note: slash_b later, still inside the live window: blade vertical overhead.
shots.name: gp_slash_b_live_late

shots._note: Charge tell: attack held past the 1067 ms threshold. Three cues, and only one of them is a colour — the held `charge` pose, an outlined teal ground ring that closes inward, and the cyan blade. The swing owns orange and the charge owns cyan, so the two can never be confused. capture_offset waits out the ring's 110 ms convergence; the charge is a held state, so any frame of it is representative.
shots.name: gp_charge_tell

shots._note: Spin, first revolution: ground ring expanding, ribbon closing into a full circle.
shots.name: gp_spin_live

shots._note: Spin, second revolution: the ring near full radius.
shots.name: gp_spin_live_late

shots._note: Showcase from here down. Useful for reading pose detail, never for judging legibility.
shots.name: show_sword_rest
